Body Text: You are entering a grocery store wearing a shirt with a Pride symbol on it. You notice another customer in the store, glaring at you. You feel isolated.
You take a moment to look around and you notice other shoppers wearing other visibly queer symbols or outfits. You realize that you are not alone.

Body Text: You are sitting in the cafeteria, when you overhear two people talking saying they think there are too many students of color being admitted to your school. You feel worried that others think you don't belong, and you feel hurt.
You recognize that they are being ignorant. You remind yourself that their opinion is not fact.
Now, it's your turn to write your own. We know discrimination can look different for everyone, so here's how you can write your own narrative.

Think about a situation where someone in appeared to be looking at you in a particular way...

Where were you when it happened? What was going on? Write about the event like it is happening now, not like it happened in the past.

Title Text: Describe Your Concerns About the Situation Initially
Body Text:
Think about what you might worry about in ways that they might be judging you, or raise the concerns you have about the situation

Some examples you can use:
I was worried about being judged. 
I thought people might not like me.
I was concerned for my safety.

Title Text: Describe How You Could Resolve Your Concern About the Situation
Body Text:
Think about what you might say to yourself about that person's judgement.

You may find it helpful to remind yourself that their judgement doesn't matter, that you are a part of community, that you are safe - or something else entirely.
Gathering your thoughts and reflecting on an experience can be a helpful way to process something difficult.
Take a moment to write out about what has been stressing you out.
